title: Embed SLI targets into quarterly roadmaps and cycle cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and operationalize a lightweight process to surface SLI targets and error budget posture directly into quarterly roadmap planning and each two-week cycle. Deliverables: a template that PMs use in planning reviews, a standard dashboard card in the Console showing current SLI vs target and remaining error budget, and a cadence (weekly/biweekly) for error-budget burn reviews tied to launch gates and canary rollouts.
background: We regularly set high-level reliability OKRs but lack a consistent way to translate SLI targets into cycle-level work and release gating. During the last incident (2025-11-12), stakeholders missed a timely rollback because the error-budget burn rate wasn't surfaced on the build dashboard. This initiative addresses that gap by making SLI data a first-class input to roadmap trade-offs and release decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A planning checklist template exists and is used by at least 3 product teams during the Q2 planning cycle
Console shows a new "SLI Snapshot" card with current SLI, target, and 14-day burn rate for selected services
Error budget alert runbook is linked from the card and contains clear escalation steps
At least one rollout in Dedicated or Hosted used the new gate with documented outcome (canary adjusted, rollback, or accept)
PMs can export a CSV of SLI vs target for quarterly OKR reviews
work_items: PM: Draft planning checklist & one-page guidance (PM-7391-01)
ENG: Add SLI Snapshot API endpoints and ensure permissioning (ENG-2843)
ENG: Implement SLI card in Console dashboard and allow embedding in route pages (ENG-2910)
DES: Design compact dashboard card and alert modal (DES-210)
PM: Run pilot with Search and Ingest teams during Cycle 3 and collect feedback
risks_and_tradeoffs: Pulling real-time SLI data into planning increases Console query load — added caching will be required to avoid spikes
Strict gating based on short-window SLI could block important feature launches; we must balance with percentage-based grace windows and manual override paths
Accuracy depends on consistent SLI definitions across services; upfront effort needed to harmonize SLI definitions which can delay rollout
